growth","USD export","Shot sculpting on Alembic caches","Flood layers","Jiggle, Muscle, Skin slide and Cloth in the Flood stack"],"notesUrl":"https://klaysculpt.com/releases/0.0.59","windows":{"url":"https://github.com/c6ank/klay-releases/releases/download/0.0.59/Klay_Setup_0.0.59.exe","size":302363886,"sha512":"071bd27de2ca0b5f5e6e33ea3570d3de62ddcce1518f6cca266488d1a332b32563c7a162e6a326b1b4d055661ff3d9c7da0c7dbbcab1caf9930352653a712172"},"mac":{"version":"0.0.59","url":"https://github.com/c6ank/klay-releases/releases/download/0.0.59/Klay_0.0.59_macOS.dmg","size":551958805,"sha512":"744bdd61f385e60b1d0283605b8294a52fd3a2c06f2bbac4ea1af4e335b630330c2aaac6c97efbd348c8f1e42e084e6f976b6d297a6d4ac478eb1c11fc6964f7"},"linux":{"version":"0.0.59","url":"https://github.com/c6ank/klay-releases/releases/download/0.0.59/Klay_0.0.59_linux_x86_64.AppImage","size":354785784,"sha512":"2b89f38bc8911f0b8a7c2c8de859d177b92a5bd12d14c63544f6275f484ec339ff0f874cb16a24438df25b3b85d6e3975a6790c44bc99edd000be1367128b518","deb":{"url":"https://github.com/c6ank/klay-releases/releases/download/0.0.59/klay_0.0.59_amd64.deb","size":372971452,"sha512":"d2fa26864cc0d2e4d731e8f9d9748e441c22926ea426b89bcb5f7cb95afcecd3bf6209f938cb6e96eca0b1c70ac4f89b1e8199246e512b61b73b7f6e00ba2f9c"},"rpm":{"url":"https://github.com/c6ank/klay-releases/releases/download/0.0.59/klay-0.0.59-1.x86_64.rpm","size":383546948,"sha512":"d74c6573a72d55976d519cf499efcc26082be8bb5649fa97c111680405f60d24e6bce3ba725d382bfd69e68a3b66ed21bbbd38ffc784755e7190891953fcfbae"}},"items":[{"g":"n","t":"Scatter tool","b":"The Scatter tool places many copies of one or more objects on surfaces or on the ground: paint them, draw them along a line or curve, fill an area, fill the inside of any mesh with Fill volume (tumbling at random or upright, kept clear of the surface), or drop them with physics so they fall and settle. Copies can be grouped, selected, filtered by slope, height or mask, grown into clusters, and scattered on top of another scatter, such as moss on scattered rocks. A set can be saved to the Library as a preset and reused in any scene, and Convert to poly turns the whole set, or one group, into meshes or instances when it is done, from the Output section or the right-click menu.","w":["Toolbar \u203a Tools \u203a Scatter"]},{"g":"n","t":"Scatter growth","b":"With Growth turned on, each copy that Paint, Fill brush or Single places becomes a seed that grows more copies. The card offers 58 recipes in a searchable list, from trees, palms and ferns to fungi, roots, coral, crystals, tentacles and snowflakes. Each recipe is tagged with its category, method and where it grows, and recipes can be saved, deleted and restored. Four Character sliders (Size, Bushiness, Reach and Wildness) adjust a recipe as a whole, and Age grows or ungrows the result. The Pieces diagram names the prototype used for each stem, split, leaf, tip and fruit, and a searchable list picks it. Fine tune covers six growth methods, including Spiral, together with radial copies, weight bend, wind lean, leaf arrangement, a drawn thickness curve, obstacles that are climbed or avoided, and growth toward a chosen light or object. Stages add later growths, such as fronds from a trunk or strands hanging from a crown. Grown copies are ordinary copies that can be erased, adjusted and undone.","w":["Scatter tool card \u203a Growth"]},{"g":"n","t":"USD export","b":"Models export to USD (.usda). Each object's geometry is written once and its copies reference it, so a mesh duplicated many times stays small and arrives as instances in other applications. Instance packs and scatters are written as point instancers. Quads, normals, UVs, vertex colours and the base colour, roughness and metallic of each material are kept.","w":["Export \u203a USD","Outliner \u203a Export as USD\u2026"]},{"g":"n","t":"Shot sculpting on Alembic caches","b":"An animated Alembic cache now appears in the outliner as a regular object card, with its own layers, fields and polygroups and the + Layer button. A new layer is keyed at full weight on the current frame. Selecting the cache or some of its layers shows their weight curves in the timeline, where keys can be added, moved and eased. Each layer's slider in the outliner scales its whole curve. The layers, their curves, polygroups and fields are saved with the scene. The cache's right-click menu lists every mesh action with its icon; actions that would change the topology are greyed out. Export sequence writes the Alembic back out with the layers applied, keeping its hierarchy, names, polygons and UVs. Replace swaps in another Alembic and keeps the work; when the new mesh differs, a dialog offers to transfer the layers to the closest point.","w":["Outliner \u203a Alembic cache \u203a + Layer","Outliner \u203a Alembic cache \u203a Export sequence\u2026","Timeline"]},{"g":"n","t":"Flood layers","b":"A Flood stack can now live in the layer list as a Flood layer. It processes the base and every layer above it, so a Flood layer at the bottom of the list acts on everything. A stroke on any layer above it shows as sculpted while the button is held, and the Flood layer updates when it is released. The Flood button on its row opens the Flood tab on that layer, where its processes can be edited; Back returns to the previous stack and Detach keeps a copy of it. Bake to sculpt layer keeps the current result as an ordinary layer. On an animated Alembic cache, Flood layers are evaluated on every shown frame while the timeline plays or is scrubbed, so every process follows the animation; a masked Flood layer computes only its masked zone. A new Flood layer starts with an empty mask and has no effect until its mask is painted: the painted area is where it applies. Flood layers are saved with the scene.","w":["Outliner \u203a Layers \u203a Flood layer","Flood \u203a Apply to \u203a New Flood layer"]},{"g":"n","t":"Jiggle, Muscle, Skin slide and Cloth in the Flood stack","b":"The Flood tab has a new Animation category with four processes that add secondary motion to an animated mesh: Jiggle for fat that bounces and settles, Muscle for a firmer wobble, Skin slide for skin that slides and wrinkles over a jiggling body, and Cloth for loose cloth. The painted mask sets where the effect applies, with a soft edge; everything outside it keeps the animation exactly. Bounce and Settle set how fast the zone oscillates and how quickly it comes to rest, and Keep volume, Max travel and Wrinkles shape the result. The processes simulate while the timeline plays and store each frame, so scrubbing shows the stored result; inside a Flood layer on an animated Alembic cache they also follow scrubbing and catch up after a jump or an edit. Only the masked zone is computed.","w":["Flood \u203a Add \u203a Animation"]},{"g":"n","t":"Primitives as clay stamps","b":"The clay Stamp brush can now stamp with a primitive from the Primitives library as well as with a custom stamp. Eight quick slots hold the shapes in use, and each slot can be changed from the library. The shape's own settings, such as width, bevel or number of sides, are available in the Stamp menu and on the tool card, and a preview above the menu shows the stamp as it changes.","w":["Toolbar \u203a Stamp \u203a Primitive","Stamp tool card \u203a Stamp \u203a Primitive","Stamp \u203a Library\u2026"]},{"g":"n","t":"SVG shapes and fonts for Text primitives","b":"A Text primitive can now use any font installed on the computer, with its styles, chosen from a searchable list that shows each font in its own face. A new SVG primitive extrudes the filled shapes of an .svg file, such as a logo, with the same size, depth, bevel and puff settings; the file can also be dropped on the viewport. The shape is saved in the scene, so it opens without the file.","w":["Primitives \u203a Text & 2D \u203a Text / SVG","Primitives \u203a Shape \u203a Source"]},{"g":"n","t":"Scene reminder","b":"The scene name in the top-left corner gradually changes colour while the scene has unsaved changes, from white to orange to red, and then glows. Its tooltip shows how long the scene has been unsaved. The time to red can be set to 5, 10, 20 or 30 minutes; saving resets it. Right-clicking the scene name saves an increment.","w":["Settings \u203a Preferences \u203a Scene reminder"]},{"g":"i","t":"Faster animated Alembic","b":"Animated Alembic files import about nine times faster, and playback at 24 and 30 fps stays in sync with the timeline. The whole clip is now kept on the graphics card when it fits, using about a fifth of the video memory per frame, so scrubbing the timeline shows every frame without waiting. The memory is released when the scene needs it.","w":["File \u203a Import \u203a Alembic","Timeline"]},{"g":"i","t":"Faster Voxelize","b":"Voxelize now prepares its shaders while the window is open, so the first Apply of a session no longer pauses, and each Apply, including the detail projection back onto the result, takes less time. The result is the same mesh as before.","w":["Right-click \u203a Process \u203a Voxelize"]},{"g":"i","t":"Clean topology for polygon primitives","b":"In the Primitives tool, the box, slab, sphere, egg, superellipsoid, capsule, disc, bipyramid, torus and round tube now build an even quad mesh when placed as polygons, with rows that follow the bevels and the rims, in place of the grid-shaped mesh. The surface is the same as the clay version of the shape. A shape with noise, a shell, a boolean or a morph keeps the previous mesh, and a line under Segments says which mesh is used.","w":["Primitives \u203a Poly mesh"]},{"g":"i","t":"Layer masks use the full Mask tool","b":"Selecting a sculpt layer's mask in the layer list now opens the Mask tool on the preset already in use, and every Mask preset works on that layer's mask exactly as on the object's mask: painting, Shift blur, Blur, Sharpen, Expand and Contract, Invert, box and lasso masks, the operators and Fill from sources. The layer mask is shown in its own tint colour. Blur, Sharpen, Expand and Invert on a layer mask now update the surface immediately.","w":["Layers \u203a Layer mask","Mask tool"]},{"g":"i","t":"Pen pressure for the Mask tool","b":"The Mask tool has the Pen pressure card of the sculpt brushes: pen pressure can drive the strength, the size and the hardness of the mask, each with its own light-touch and full-press values and its own response curve. A preset that used the former Pressure switch keeps pressure on its strength.","w":["Mask tool \u203a Pen pressure"]},{"g":"i","t":"Smoother clay stamps","b":"Custom clay stamps now keep a smooth surface when deposited at a large brush size, where they previously showed fine banding.","w":["Clay \u203a Stamp brush"]},{"g":"i","t":"Edit several primitives at once","b":"In the Primitives tool, several primitives can be selected from the outliner or with hold-V (click, or drag a rectangle; Ctrl removes). When they are the same shape, the primitive's handles and card edit all of them: move, rotate and scale apply to each one, and a bevel or other setting takes the same value on every selected primitive. When the shapes differ, the gizmo moves, rotates and scales them together. Each change is one undo step.","w":["Primitives \u203a Outliner / hold V"]},{"g":"i","t":"Primitive copies and instances","b":"In the Primitives tool, Ctrl+D makes an independent copy of a primitive, and Ctrl-dragging the centre handle, an axis arrow or a plane handle makes a copy and moves it (Alt-drag with Ctrl and Alt swapped). Right-click \u203a Instance makes a linked copy instead: a shape change on any instance applies to all of them, while each keeps its own position. Unlink copy in the outliner makes an instance independent.","w":["Primitives \u203a Ctrl+D / Ctrl+drag","Right-click \u203a Instance","Outliner \u203a Unlink copy"]},{"g":"i","t":"Join controls on clay primitives","b":"A clay primitive now shows three arcs around its centre handle in the Primitives tool: one sets Add, Subtract or Intersect, one the blend radius, and one the blend: each of its stops shows the blend's icon from the join settings (Round, Chamfer, Muscle, Groove, Weld, Inflate). The radius arc takes the colour of the current operation. Drag along an arc, click a stop, or use the mouse wheel over it. Each change is one undo step and matches the join settings in the outliner. The blend radius goes from 0 to 10 on the arc and in the join settings, with the first three quarters of each slider covering 0 to 5.","w":["Primitives \u203a Viewport \u203a Join arcs"]},{"g":"i","t":"Selected clay primitive highlight","b":"In the Primitives tool, the selected clay primitive now shows a faint tint on the part of the clay it forms, with a thin outline, so it can be told apart where it blends into other shapes. Every selected primitive is highlighted, and the highlight is hidden while a primitive is being dragged or edited.","w":["Primitives \u203a Viewport"]},{"g":"i","t":"New primitives sit on the face they are drawn from","b":"Dragging out a new primitive from a surface now stands it on that surface: drawn from the side of a box, it stands on that side. On a primitive, a slightly rounded or bevelled face counts as flat. The new primitive also takes the rotation of the object it is drawn on, so its edges line up with that object's edges at any camera angle. Hold Shift while dragging to place it upright, as before.","w":["Primitives \u203a Drag to place"]},{"g":"i","t":"Lattice density with + and \u2212","b":"In the Lattice tool, + and \u2212 add or remove one row of control points on all three axes at once. The current deformation is kept, and each press is one undo step.","w":["Tools \u203a Lattice"]},{"g":"i","t":"Lattice applies to sculpt layers","b":"When a sculpt layer is selected on a mesh, Apply puts the lattice deformation into that layer instead of the base mesh. With several meshes caged, each mesh receives it in the layer last selected on it. The Apply on new layer option creates a layer named Lattice on every caged mesh instead. One undo step reverses the whole Apply.","w":["Tools \u203a Lattice"]},{"g":"i","t":"Create a scatter set from the menu","b":"Create \u203a Scatter set makes a scatter set from the selected objects and opens the Scatter tool on it. With nothing selected, the set starts empty. It replaces Create \u203a Instance pack, and Instance point is no longer listed in the menus.","w":["Right-click \u203a Create \u203a Scatter set"]},{"g":"i","t":"Faster scatters of small objects","b":"Scatters and duplicated copies of objects with fewer than 20,000 triangles now use the same level of detail as large meshes, so thousands of small props draw several times fewer triangles at a distance. Display \u203a Mesh \u203a Display cluster \u203a Scatter override gives scatters their own detail threshold, one for perspective and one for orthographic views, without changing other meshes. The level-of-detail colour view shows the same range of levels on copies as on the original mesh.","w":["Tools \u203a Scatter"]},{"g":"i","t":"Clay volume box shows when its size changes","b":"Pointing at a resolution in the outliner's Resolution menu shows the clay layer's volume box in the viewport, together with the size of the box that resolution gives. Shift+D and Shift+F briefly fade the box in and out, on clay layers and primitive layers alike.","w":["Outliner \u203a Resolution"]},{"g":"i","t":"Even smoothing on mixed-density meshes","b":"The Smooth section of a polygon brush has a new Topology aware option, next to Smooth passes. When it is on, dense and low-resolution areas are smoothed at the same rate, so low-resolution areas no longer flatten faster than the detailed areas beside them.","w":["Brush \u203a Smooth \u203a Topology aware"]},{"g":"i","t":"Shader compile count on the splash screen","b":"When Klay has to compile its shaders at start, for example on the first launch on macOS or Linux or after a graphics driver update, the splash screen shows the progress as Compiling shaders with a count, in place of the version number. A normal start is unchanged.","w":["Start \u203a Splash screen"]},{"g":"i","t":"Studio seats without a setup step","b":"When KLAY_LICENSE_SERVER is set in the environment Klay is launched from, Klay connects to that licence server at launch and takes a seat, as other pipeline applications do; its address takes priority over the one saved in Settings. On a workstation where IT has deployed klay_server.json, Klay switches to studio mode at start without anyone opening Settings, and a Connect or Disconnect chosen by hand is kept.","w":["Settings \u203a Licence \u203a Studio server"]},{"g":"i","t":"Export Stop Motion matches the Export window","b":"The Export Stop Motion dialog now uses the same layout as the Export / Import window, with one tile per format and the file names above the buttons. Its options and behaviour are unchanged.","w":["Outliner \u203a Right-click a recording \u203a Export Stop Motion\u2026"]},{"g":"i","t":"Animated start screen","b":"The start screen now drops into place and settles with a short bounce, followed by the pieces of the logo, the Klay name and the version. While Klay loads, each piece of the logo swells slightly as it fills and settles with a small bounce.","w":["Launch"]},{"g":"f","t":"Switching from a stamp brush to Smooth and back, with Shift or the VR trigger, no longer causes a short frame drop."},{"g":"f","t":"In VR, the Spray can stays active when it points past the model. The cone and the outline on the surface remain visible, and the part of the spray circle that still touches the clay keeps smoothing or painting."},{"g":"f","t":"The Stamp menu above the toolbar now closes when you click elsewhere, unless it is pinned. The Stamp label opens the stamp library on the brush's current kind, Custom or Primitive. The stamp picker on the sidebar's tool card now shows only on the clay Stamp brush, and no longer stays after you switch to a surface or polygon brush."},{"g":"f","t":"The Scene totals line of the viewport HUD now counts scatter copies and their triangles. Before, a scatter set counted as one object with no triangles."},{"g":"f","t":"Typing in the toolbar drawer's search now only highlights the matching tool. Before, each letter switched to the first match, so typing R selected the Planar tool. Press Enter or click a result to select it."},{"g":"f","t":"Dragging a key up or down in the timeline is now one undo step. Before, every small move of the drag was stored separately."},{"g":"f","t":"Painting a mask, or sculpting, on an animated Alembic cache after the timeline has moved no longer leaves blocky, cut-off patches."},{"g":"f","t":"The mask brush's Topology reach now works on an animated Alembic cache after the timeline has moved. Before, it masked nothing."},{"g":"f","t":"An animated Alembic cache made of quads now shows a quad wireframe, as a static import does, instead of triangles. A cache imported before this version is converted again the first time it is loaded."},{"g":"f","t":"Polygon brushes now work in the orthographic view when you are zoomed in close. Before, Draw and many other brushes dented the surface instead of building it up, or did nothing at all. Grab and Move on polygon and clay objects, and dragging lights, fields and Layout items, now also follow the cursor in the orthographic view; before, nothing moved."},{"g":"f","t":"A large Draw stroke on a dense polygon mesh no longer leaves square, blocky patches in the deposit. The stroke now stays smooth at any brush size and strength."},{"g":"f","t":"Cloth brushes such as Blow no longer slow down on a dense polygon mesh. A small stroke now uses memory for the area it touches instead of the whole mesh, and the rest of the model keeps its level of detail while you sculpt."},{"g":"f","t":"Visiting an exhibition no longer changes your own settings: its dust, fog, sky and other atmosphere effects stay in the exhibition and are gone when you leave it, including after a restart. During a visit, brushes and tools are off and the mouse only moves the view, so the work can no longer be sculpted."},{"g":"f","t":"Saving a very large polygon mesh with sculpt layers no longer crashes Klay when GPU memory is nearly full."},{"g":"f","t":"A polygon primitive now keeps smooth, even shading while you drag its handles or after you edit it, instead of showing blotchy patches."},{"g":"f","t":"Installing Klay now prepares the shaders for Solas, MatCap, the remesh preview and the material effects, so they no longer pause the first time they are used. The installer shows how many shaders it has built. A material that combines effects in a new way, such as subsurface scattering with specular, no longer freezes Klay: it is shown right away and refines a few seconds later."},{"g":"f","t":"Subsurface scattering now follows the object's scale: a scaled mesh keeps the same translucent look instead of turning opaque or glowing, in both the viewport and Raytrace."},{"g":"f","t":"In the Unlit view, the back faces of an open mesh are now lit instead of black, so the inside of a shell stays readable."},{"g":"f","t":"Leaving the Tessellation tool no longer freezes Klay, and neither does Optimize IDs on a polygon mesh."},{"g":"f","t":"The scale ring around a primitive's centre handle no longer loses part of its circle when the scene contains measurements."},{"g":"f","t":"A Wacom pen side button set to Middle click in the Wacom driver no longer opens the right-click menu on a short press, with or without Shift or Ctrl (macOS)."},{"g":"f","t":"After aligning a primitive on a clay layer, the Align tool's face highlight now follows the new surface instead of showing scrambled faces until the tool was restarted."},{"g":"f","t":"Opening Klay no longer turns off the desktop's window effects (blur, shadows, transparency) while it runs (Linux)."},{"g":"f","t":"Mirror with the World plane now uses the world axis on a rotated object, and a Live instance made this way stays mirrored across that plane when the original is moved. With the Object plane, Mirror and the sculpt symmetry go through a custom pivot placed by hand; Pivot at Bottom no longer moves the plane. A Custom plane now follows the object when it moves."},{"g":"f","t":"With Edit pivot on in the Gizmo tool, typing a rotation or pasting in the Transform card or the outliner Transform panel turns only the pivot, not the mesh. Pivot changes can now be undone."},{"g":"f","t":"In the Primitive and Primitives tools, F and Frame selected now frame the selected primitive instead of its whole clay layer, and the camera orbits around it. A frames clay primitive layers by their primitives, not by their layer box."},{"g":"f","t":"The + and \u2212 keys now resize the Primitives tool's handles, as they do for the gizmo."},{"g":"f","t":"Joins between clay primitives keep their size and shape when the layer's box is tightened or loosened with Shift+D or Shift+F. The Inflate join's depth now follows its radius, so existing Inflate joins appear deeper."},{"g":"f","t":"A round cylinder or tube scaled along one side now becomes an oval instead of a rounded box."},{"g":"f","t":"With Right-drag rotates off in the Primitives tool, right-clicking a primitive opens Swap shape again instead of the general menu, and right-dragging turns the view."},{"g":"f","t":"Primitive mirroring now uses the correct World and Object planes on rotated or scaled layers. A mirrored primitive keeps its Instance X / Y / Z state after its layer is moved, so its twins can still be edited or removed."},{"g":"f","t":"The Symmetry options open reliably from the side bar, including with the sidebar on the left and the button names shown; right-clicking the button also opens them, and Shift + right-click replaces it."},{"g":"f","t":"Collapsing or joining a mirrored copy now keeps a clean, upright frame and puts its pivot on the mirrored side."},{"g":"f","t":"With Environment > Floor on, rough materials no longer reflect a sharp floor edge near the horizon; their reflection now stays as soft as their roughness."},{"g":"f","t":"Klay no longer recompiles its shaders when you start it again after closing it, or after switching between the desktop and VR. Compiled shaders are now kept separately for each mode."},{"g":"f","t":"In VR, grabbing and turning the model follows the hands smoothly on heavy scenes and during fast movements, instead of lagging and catching up in jumps. Resizing a brush with the thumbstick no longer lowers the frame rate."}],"history":[{"version":"0.0.58","date":"2026-11-03","lede":"Faster primitive editing: an optional raymarching shader draws clay primitives while you edit them, so moving them no longer rebuilds the clay every frame","highlights":["Faster primitive editing","Mirror a placed primitive"],"notesUrl":"https://klaysculpt.com/releases/0.0.58","items":[{"g":"n","t":"Faster primitive editing","b":"With Raymarching when editing turned on, a clay layer of primitives is drawn by a raymarching shader while one of its primitives is moved, resized or edited, instead of rebuilding the clay every frame, so editing stays smooth with many primitives and with any material. When the edit stops, only the part of the clay that changed is rebuilt, once, and the layer is drawn from its mesh again; the selection outline stays visible throughout. The option is off by default; Raymarch all primitive layers in the same section draws these layers by raymarching at all times.","w":["Display settings \u203a Raymarching \u203a Raymarching when editing"]},{"g":"n","t":"Mirror a placed primitive","b":"The Primitives card has a Mirror section. Instance X, Y and Z add a linked mirrored copy of the selected primitive across the symmetry plane of that axis, and a second click removes it; editing either side changes both. With Follow symmetry on, turning symmetry on mirrors the selected primitive straight away.","w":["Primitives \u203a Mirror"]},{"g":"i","t":"Bevels keep their size when primitives are resized","b":"A primitive with a bevel or rounded edges keeps the same bevel on every side, at the same size, when it is made larger with the size handles, Scale X / Y / Z or the gizmo: a cube stretched into a rectangle keeps even edges, and a stretched disc or tube becomes a slot. The bevel only becomes smaller when the primitive is made smaller than its original size. On shapes with repeated details, such as gear teeth, text, bricks and window bars, the axes that cross those details still stretch as before.","w":["Tools \u203a Primitives"]},{"g":"i","t":"Primitive handles: move in a plane, resize one side","b":"The centre handle now matches the Gizmo tool: its dot moves the primitive in the screen plane, its ring scales it, and three plane dots move it within one plane (XY, YZ or ZX). Hold Shift while dragging a size handle to move only that side, while the opposite side stays in place; Ctrl now gives fine adjustment on size handles.","w":["Tools \u203a Primitives"]},{"g":"i","t":"Pin the outliner's Display and Transform windows","b":"The Display window (opened from an object's icon) and the Transform window of the outliner now have a title bar like the Blending window: drag it to move the window anywhere, including over the viewport. The pin button beside the close button keeps the window open; clicking another object's icon or transform button then shows that object in the same window. The Transform window now updates once an edit is finished rather than during it.","w":["Outliner \u203a Object icon / Transform"]},{"g":"i","t":"More blends for Subtract and Intersect, Type and curve on every blend","b":"Muscle, Groove, Weld, Inflate, Columns, Stairs, Split edge, Noisy, Sag and Stretch now also work with Subtract and Intersect, shaping the rim of the cut; Weld, Muscle and Inflate still add material there. The blend Type (Smooth, Chamfer, Soft, Circular, Silky, Exact) now changes the Columns, Stairs, Pipe, Muscle and Inflate blends too: Chamfer gives diamond pleats, bevelled steps or a diamond tube, and the other types round them differently. The Type row is hidden on Chamfer and Morph, where it has no effect. The profile curve is available on every blend except Chamfer, Pipe and Morph: with the Smooth type it sets the shape of the join, and on Inflate the shape of the puff. Each blend of a primitive now keeps the last values you gave it, also after restarting Klay; Reset blend returns it to its defaults.","w":["Outliner \u203a Blending"]},{"g":"i","t":"Primitive noise through Noise layers only","b":"The Primitives card no longer has the Surface and Noise advanced sections; noise and patterns are added with Noise layers. A primitive from an older scene that already has a surface noise still shows those sections, so the noise can be edited or removed.","w":["Tools \u203a Primitives \u203a Noise layers"]},{"g":"f","t":"Resizing the tool card in the sidebar by its top handle no longer stutters in scenes with many layers."},{"g":"f","t":"The Swap shape list now opens at the selected primitive's shape and highlights it, instead of at the top."},{"g":"f","t":"Dragging a slider on the Primitives card, or moving, rotating or scaling a primitive in the viewport, no longer makes the viewport stutter."}]},{"version":"0.0.57","date":"2026-11-02","lede":"Clay paint colour and material from the toolbar, and Klay starts again on AMD Radeon RX 5000 and RX 6000 cards","highlights":["Clay paint colour and material","Colour for clay primitives","Noise layers for primitives"],"notesUrl":"https://klaysculpt.com/releases/0.0.57","items":[{"g":"n","t":"Clay paint colour and material","b":"The clay row of the toolbar has a Color tile between Stamp and Stencil, showing the paint on a small lit ball; click it to turn the paint on or off. Hover it to pick a colour, and use the palette's expand button or the tile's label for the Clay paint panel: colour, albedo, roughness, metal and emission, strength, softening, jitter or a gradient along the stroke, and colour smudging. From surface picks the colour of painted clay with a click, and pen pressure can drive the albedo strength, the jitter amount or the gradient colour. Painted clay no longer tints the rest of the model, and brushes that drip, such as Melting, carry the paint they drip from, tinted by the paint colour at its strength. The palette and the panel can be pinned and moved, and the colour cell of the zen Brush pastille opens the same palette and panel.","w":["Toolbar \u203a Clay \u203a Color"]},{"g":"n","t":"Colour for clay primitives","b":"Clay primitives have a Color section with three switches: Albedo with a colour, Roughness and Metalness, each with its value.
